decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its target federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 6 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee voted today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 6 percent.
changes.explanation: The central bank pushed its main interest rate up from 5-3/4 percent to 6 percent to slow down economic overheating.

changes.quote: Economic conditions and considerations addressed by the Committee are essentially the same as when the Committee met in February.
changes.explanation: Policymakers stated that the overall economic picture has remained largely unchanged since their prior meeting.

changes.quote: The Committee remains concerned that increases in demand will continue to exceed the growth in potential supply, which could foster inflationary imbalances that would undermine the economy's record economic expansion.
changes.explanation: The Fed modified its language while reiterating that rapid growth in demand compared to supply could trigger unwanted inflation.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee remains concerned that increases in demand will continue to exceed the growth in potential supply, which could foster inflationary imbalances that would undermine the economy's record economic expansion.

Against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the Committee believes the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate heightened inflation pressures in the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.12% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate; with the 10-year at 6.13% moving -5 bp on the day, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 8.23% would fall by about $10.53 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 218k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.2% over the past year (February 2000); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.

whats_next: The Fed highlighted that inflation risks remain tilted to the upside due to strong demand pressures. Educational forecasts indicate that additional interest rate hikes may be needed if demand continues to outpace potential supply.
